In ACC After Dark action, Stanford hosts NC State at Stanford Stadium in Stanford, Calif., on Friday at 10:30 p.m. ET (ESPN). The Wolfpack are 6.5-point road favorites, and my NC State vs. Stanford prediction and college football picks expect CJ Bailey to pick apart one of the Power Four's worst defenses. TOP PICK Who will win NC State vs Stanford: NC State -6.5 Stanford has been completely uncompetitive in four of its last five FBS games and is 1-5 ATS since the start of September. While NC State isn't a powerhouse, the Wolfpack have enough offense to cover up to -8.5 on the road . The Cardinal have lost four of their last five FBS games by at least 28 points and scored seven or fewer in all four (they were outscored 115-10 in their last two FBS games) . With a defense that's ranked 127th in success rate (50.1%) , Stanford's offense won't be able to keep up with the Wolfpack. NC State has scored 31+ points in three of its last four FBS games, all against defenses ranked higher by SP+ than Stanford's (111th). Plus, the Wolfpack are coming off a bye week and should be well rested for the West Coast trip. NC State vs Stanford Over/Under pick: Over 55.5 NC State and Stanford have struggling defenses, which have helped them consistently hit the Over this season. The Wolfpack and Cardinal are a combined 9-4 to the Over, and I like it to hit at 55.5 or better . Stanford's defense has the lowest havoc rate in the ACC (11.3%) and is allowing the second-most yards per game in the Power Four (452) . NC State's defense isn't all that much better, though, ranking 124th in net EPA per play and 133rd in EPA per pass. These two defenses bend and break, ranking the worst in the conference in points per opportunity on defense, though Stanford (5.06) is significantly worse than NC State (3.94). NC State vs Stanford combo Stanford is one of the worst teams in college football, and it doesn't look like Andrew Luck and Tavita Pritchard will be turning things around anytime soon. Though Davis Warren has been efficient at QB, the Cardinal have a dreadful defense that ranks outside the top 115 in EPA per pass, EPA per rush, and available yards percentage (57.3%). Even against an NC State defense giving up 27.7 points per game, Stanford won't be able to keep this close at home against David Doeren's team. The Wolfpack's passing game will be too much, and I have NC State winning 33-24 . However, win, and there's a chance to go on a big second-half run with a favorable schedule. Stanford is trying to fight the good fight in a rebuild under new head coach Tavita Pritchard, but at 3-4 with only one home game left, it's in big trouble if it loses. NC State vs Stanford: Quick Hits Why does Stanford need this? Three straight road games follow this, but that includes a trip up the road to Cal. NC State only has one game – at Florida State – outside of North Carolina the rest of the way, hosting Cal, Duke, and Syracuse next. The two programs have only met once. The lack of a pass rush and few defensive stops are the real issues, but you can't win if you don't score, and Stanford can't put the biscuit in the basket. Not to get all basic here, but the Cardinal have scored seven points or fewer in the four losses, and 34 or more in the three wins. The ground game has been non-existent against everyone but Elon and Hawaii. NC State is fantastic at keeping the chains moving. Stanford doesn't get to the quarterback and will struggle to hit Wolfpack star CJ Bailey enough to get off the field. Why Stanford Will Win Okay, context time. Yeah, Stanford's offense was putrid in the four losses. One of those came against a nasty Duke defense Durham, and the other three losses were to Miami, Notre Dame, and a Wake Forest team whose only loss is to the Hurricanes. This is one of those focus-test moments for the ACC team from the Eastern Time Zone. This will end around 2 am NC State time, and while these are college kids who can certainly stay awake, the rhythm will be thrown off. NC State vs Stanford Prediction, Betting Lines Don't just blow this off as a layup win for NC State before getting back on the plane to go deal with bigger and better things. The Wolfpack have had to deal with a whole ton of adversity this season, and they keep coming back, but it's 0-2 on the road, and Stanford is 3-1 at home, with that one loss coming to Miami. NC State doesn't have the pass rush to overwhelm the Cardinal backfield, but it'll be just okay enough to get out with a tough late-night win. away.headline: Stanford Injury Report Ahead of Season-Defining Matchup With NC State
away.blurb: But the program needs to get by without some key players. Ahead of the matchup, the ACC released official injury reports for this week. Stanford has multiple players still listed out, including linebacker Matt Rose and defensive back Brandon Nicholson. He has played at an elite level when healthy, but it is still to be disclosed how long he will be out. Stanford needs him back desperately to improve linebacker depth and production. Rose is the leader of the defense, and his presence elevates everyone around him. He's set to miss a significant amount of time, and it is highly possible that he will not return this season, putting the program in a tough spot. After Collin Wright missed time with an injury of his own last season, Nicholson shined and proved himself as a key player for the defense. Defensive backs Lonnie McAllister III and Chris Garland are questionable, while Lasiah Jackson is probable. NC State will be down some key stars as well. Running back Jayden Scott, defensive back Tristan Teasdell and tight end Vander Ploog headline the list of injured NC State players. Scott, NC State's leading rusher, has 62 carries for 358 yards and four touchdowns this season. With him out, it will be interesting to see how the Wolfpack's offense attacks. Wide receiver Jojo Trader and offensive tackle Kamen Smith are listed as questionable for the Wolfpack. If they return, they will provide a big boost. This game is big for both teams. For Stanford, a win puts them back at .500 and digs them out of a massive hole when it comes to returning to a bowl game. They would reach four wins, which is their total from last season, and would have a path to reaching a bowl game. That path evaporates with a loss. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 6 Indiana looks to rebound from a loss to Ohio State, while Michigan begins again at quarterback Getty Images The Tommy Carr era in Ann Arbor will officially get underway this Saturday when the freshman quarterback makes his first career start at home against No. 6 Indiana . Carr led a second-half comeback last week against Penn State after former five-star recruit Bryce Underwood was benched, and Michigan made the decision to fully turn the operation over to Carr against an extremely good Indiana defense. That will present a major challenge for Carr, but it also shows Michigan's faith in him as the best option against the defending champs. Indiana comes into the game trying to shake off the frustration of a loss at home to Ohio State last week, coming a literal foot away from a win had Nick Marsh been able to keep his feet in bounds on a wide-open fourth-down pass from Josh Hoover . The Hoosiers need to refocus after the disappointment of their first loss in two years, as they head into the Big House to face a Michigan team that may not be elite on offense but will still present a stiff test for an Indiana offense that's been out of sync recently. The Hoosiers are 7.5-point road favorites, but the Wolverines suddenly have a bit of life after last week's win, and the excitement for a new quarterback will create a lively atmosphere in Ann Arbor. Michigan vs. Indiana: Need to know Tommy Carr's first start: Carr took over for Bryce Underwood at halftime against Penn State and performed solidly, leading three Michigan touchdown drives -- that came off three Penn State turnovers. While he only threw for 47 yards, playing complementary football and cashing in on great defensive plays to turn them into points is a major step forward for this Michigan offense. However, doing that against a bad Penn State team is one thing; now Carr will face an Indiana defense that's among the best in the country. He'll be tasked with not turning the ball over and taking what's in front of him, but Indiana will know that as well, and Michigan might have to let Carr turn it loose a couple of times down the field if they're going to force the Hoosiers off the line of scrimmage. Michigan knows this will be an extremely difficult first start for Carr and will likely try to protect him with quick concepts and a run-heavy approach, but if they want to pull off the upset, Carr is going to have to deliver a couple big plays Indiana's not expecting. Can Indiana establish a rhythm?: A stop-start offense has been a problem all season for Indiana, and while they escaped the first six games without it costing them, it finally caught up in Columbus. Now they face a Michigan defense that is also excellent and will present plenty of challenges, and Josh Hoover will have to prove he can move the ball consistently through the air. Indiana's offense has been predicated much more on the big play than they'd like this season, as Hoover has been able to create explosives in the passing game to Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh. However, consistency has been lacking, and that's kept the Hoosiers from pulling away from opponents as they did a year ago. Against Ohio State, Hoover threw for 296 yards, but completed just 20 of 40 passes to do so. He will need to figure out how to be sharper in the underneath and intermediate passing game if Indiana's going to have a chance of repeating, and that starts this week given the challenge Michigan will present up front. Elite run defenses: The Hoosiers and Wolverines are two of the nation's best defenses against the run, and that presents real problems for offenses that want to lean on their rushing attacks. Indiana struggled to get anything going against Ohio State, even with Turbo Richard back in the lineup, and they'll be up against it again with a Michigan defense that allows a paltry 2.68 yards per carry. One of the six teams better than Michigan against the run is Indiana, allowing just 2.28 yards per carry, which will put even more pressure on Carr to produce through the air in his first start. The team that can establish some kind of ground game will gain an advantage in this one, but there's a real possibility that neither can break through the walls of these defensive fronts. Where to watch Michigan vs. Indiana live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Michigan Stadium -- Ann Arbor, Michigan TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Michigan vs. Indiana prediction, picks We've got two elite run defenses, one inconsistent passing attack and one freshman making his first start. That is a recipe for a low-scoring battle. Michigan has played five games against teams not named UTEP , and all five games have finished with fewer than 40 points. Indiana's last two games have finished in the 30s as well, as they've faced the two best defenses on their schedule thus far, and it's hard to see a game flow here leading to anything approaching a shootout. The fear here is the potential for defensive scores, but even so, give me the under in Ann Arbor for the second straight week. Indiana suffered its first loss since the 2024 season last weekend after Ohio State won by inches. Michigan is set to turn the ball over to Tommy Carr, who replaced Bryce Underwood in the second half last week against Penn State. How will Carr and the Wolverines fare against Curt Cignetti's team? picks.headline: 3 bold predictions for Indiana football vs. Michigan: Josh Hoover will have a day
picks.blurb: Indiana (6-1, 3-1 Big Ten), for the first time in a long time, is looking to get back on track. It’ll have an opportunity to do just that at Michigan (4-2, 1-2 Big Ten) after falling last week to Ohio State at home. Can the Hoosiers do it ? That would be a hard yes if two of these bold predictions come true and one doesn’t. 3 bold predictions for Indiana at Michigan Michigan doesn’t score a touchdown The Wolverines, despite their abysmal offense through the first half of the season, have scored at least two touchdowns in every Big Ten game thus far. Expect that streak to be snapped by Indiana. The Hoosiers are simply a different test than anything Michigan has seen. True freshman Tommy Carr is poised to get his first career start on Saturday. And while it may be the best decision for the Wolverines, it couldn’t come against a tougher opponent. Indiana is going to speed Carr up, force Michigan to rely on its ground attack and then bottle that up (currently surrendering a Big Ten-best 2.3 yards per carry and just 75.4 total yards per game). The Wolverines might be able to trek into Hoosiers territory on occasion, but never into the end zone. The Hoosiers don’t crack 100 yards on the ground A few signs point in the right direction for Indiana’s run game on Saturday (at least from a total-yardage perspective). First of all, the Hoosiers run the ball a lot – and they’ve been very good at it in the Curt Cignetti era. In Indiana’s first two Big Ten outings, it registered 271 yards and 329 yards on the ground, respectively. Also, against Michigan, the expectation is that the Hoosiers should be leading most of the game. And there is no better way to nurse a lead than run the football. On the flip side, though, Indiana has managed a combined 138 rushing yards on 51 carries over the past two games. The offensive line has failed to get any push and the running backs haven’t been able to find any holes. Chunk plays, explosive plays – the Hoosiers can’t get anything positive (didn’t even have a single rush over 10 yards against Ohio State). The other bad news: Michigan’s rushing defense is elite. It allows just 2.7 yards per carry and 89.7 yards per game. This, unfortunately for Indiana, is a stoppable-force-meets-immovable-object scenario. Josh Hoover throws for three touchdowns Save for the Rutgers win – which, should that even count as Big Ten play? – quarterback Josh Hoover hasn’t thrown for three touchdowns in a league game. That may be set to change on Saturday, though. Michigan’s defense is flat-out dominant. But its lone vulnerability is defending the pass. Iowa’s Hank Brown threw for 227 yards and two scores. Penn State’s Rocco Becht slung it for 267 yards and a touchdown through the air. And, all due respect to both of those gunslingers, but neither is at the same level as Hoover, nor do they have the unreal weapons Hoover has on the outside. Expect Hoover and his stud wide receiver duo of Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh to feast against Michigan, especially considering the ongoing rushing struggles for the Hoosiers’ offense. The Michigan Wolverines got the job done in Week 7 against Penn State, and they're home again in Week 8 in what is one of the toughest games on the regular season schedule for them. If Michigan wants to keep any hopes of being in the College Football Playoff this season, they're going to have to defeat the Indiana Hoosiers on Saturday. Indiana is coming off a narrow loss to Ohio State, but they remain a top-10 team in the country and present a tough task for the Wolverines. Ahead of the game between Michigan and the Hoosiers, the college football staff here at A to Z Sports has some predictions on how this one will go. Indiana 28, Michigan 17 The Hoosiers played well enough to win against an Ohio State team that didn't play well last week, but came up just short. Losing two in a row would be a tough stretch for Indiana, and I don't think it will happen. Charlie Becker confirmed he is one of the best wideouts in the country last week and he's going to present a big problem to Michigan's defense with Nick Marsh on the other side. Michigan's defense is a good unit, but so is Indiana's, and I think it leads to the Wolverines having their defense on the field a ton. Michigan is still going to struggle to put up points with Tommy Carr at quarterback over Bryce Underwood , and it's not going to be enough to beat Indiana. - Brandon Little, A to Z Sports Ohio State Indiana 31, Michigan 20 I know there is a buzz growing in Ann Arbor after the move to Tommy Carr at quarterback, but I don't see a world where Curt Cignetti's Hoosiers drop two in a row after winning 22 straight. The truth is, Ohio State is just a much better football team than Indiana, and the Buckeyes should have won by multiple scores. The same should be true with Indiana and Michigan. I know that Carr will bring optimism, but he hasn't seen a defense like that of the Hoosiers. Not to mention, Josh Hoover and the offense will be looking for a bounce-back performance. I thought Hoover struggled for much of the game against OSU, and obviously everyone has seen Nick Marsh's gaffe at the end. They won 22 games in a row, and a national championship, but this team is much different than last year's squad. Josh Hoover takes advantage of the matchup, connecting with Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh for several explosive plays that quickly put the Hoosiers in control. Indiana dictates the pace from the opening kickoff, builds an early lead and forces Michigan to play from behind. The Wolverines have enough talent to make things interesting, but asking a true freshman quarterback to step into this situation and keep pace with Indiana is a difficult task. Carr will likely have some growing pains, and the Hoosiers should be able to capitalize on those moments while keeping Michigan's offense from finding a consistent rhythm. Hoover doesn't need to do anything spectacular throughout the entire game, but a few big throws to Becker and Marsh will make the difference. Indiana's ability to establish control early allows it to dictate the game script in the second half, forcing Michigan to take chances offensively. The Wolverines find a way to add some points late, but Indiana's early advantage proves too much to overcome. - Ryan Roberts, A to Z Sports Notre Dame This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. picks.headline: ESPN analysts predict Michigan-Indiana, weigh in on Tommy Carr
picks.blurb: ESPN analysts predict Michigan-Indiana, weigh in on Tommy Carr - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview ESPN analysts predict Michigan-Indiana, weigh in on Tommy Carr Isaiah Hole, Wolverines Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 9:50 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's going to be interesting this weekend when Michigan football hosts Indiana, given that the offense came alive with the quarterback switch from Bryce Underwood to Tommy Carr in the second half vs. Penn State . Given that the defense has been solid, if not elite (the Wolverines have the top-rated defense in yards per play), it should keep the game interesting, but if the offense can suddenly move? That could be a game-changer. On the ESPN College GameDay podcast on Wednesday, Dan Wetzel discussed the change, and noted that, in the wide-open Big Ten, the Wolverines aren't exactly out of it. "Michigan team that looked totally dead in the water until halftime of last week and may still be," Wetzel said. "But if Tommy Carr came in, they moved the offense -- he's still a true freshman, I'm not expecting a ton out of this, I don't expect this to happen. But if that sparks it -- there's no doubt that Michigan's got a defense, they've got some running backs. They could get this thing going and be at least a tough team to beat. Can spring some upsets, if not still -- conceivably, I mean, it's on the table and get to 10-2. So there's all sorts of different possibilities. And the Big Ten can make a really interesting race just in that league." That said, Wetzel does believe that the maize and blue will get their third loss this week with the Hoosiers coming to town. But, he does think that the game will be a bit closer than people would have thought just a few short weeks ago. "I'm intrigued as anything about what Michigan does at quarterback," Wetzel said. "Will both guys play: Underwood and Carr? Will they play both at the same time? You know, Utah, I said, Utah runs a two-quarterback system. That's where Whittingham came from. There was a definite spark and some competency and, like, reading run options and RPOs and different things, coming into a game and then starting a game or two different things. There's Whittingham trying to be coy about who's going to start. "How does Underwood respond to all of this? He was a very good teammate on the sideline. Does he come back if he gets back in the game and make some plays? So I'm very interested in what Michigan does. And I think they haven't been interesting all year because they haven't been able to do anything offensively, but I think they're interesting. "I think this is the worst possible opponent they could be playing is Indiana. They need a couple of turnovers. They need some penalties. They need a returned kick a bunch and keep this game low scoring to make it work. And I don't think Indiana is going to give them that. So I'll take the Hoosiers, but fascinating game for the Wolverines, no matter how the result ends up." Rece Davis agrees on all counts. But he thinks this could be a game where the maize and blue find at least some semblance of identity, but can't quite get over the hump of beating the defending national champion. "It's a great opportunity for Michigan, for sure," Davis said. "A great opportunity for Kyle Whittingham to sort of reestablish some confidence in the fan base, but the spot is wrong. The team is wrong that they're facing. I can't see Michigan with Tommy Carr or Bryce Underwood based on what we've seen from them offensively, doing enough to have a chance to win the game. They'll need some mistakes from Indiana. That's uncharacteristic. "I would assume even if Hoover isn't able to go full speed, they certainly don't have a guy that's experienced at Indiana, but I think their backup is Grant Wilson. I believe he's played, you know, he's an older guy. They'll have them coached up and ready. I think Indiana sort of methodically wins the game. I don't think they blow them out. It's going to be like a lot of the Michigan games we've seen and probably a lot like, maybe not quite as dramatic, but in final score, probably something somewhat similar to what we saw in Bloomington on Saturday between Indiana and Ohio State . I'll take the Hoosiers to roll." Michigan and Indiana kick off at 12:10 p.m. EDT, with the game set to be broadcast on Fox. away.headline: Ohio State survived Indiana, but Julian Sayin's injury may decide the Buckeyes' season
away.blurb: But that stride was debilitating. Marsh's left foot came down out of bounds, and he knew it immediately. The look on his face was heartbreaking. That misery wasn't felt on the Ohio State sideline. Instead, it was relief, but with questions about what's to come. The primary reason Indiana had a chance to win the game late was that Ohio State's starting QB Julian Sayin was knocked out of the game with an apparent right arm injury earlier in the fourth quarter. Ohio State coach Ryan Day said after the game, without going into specifics about the injury, that Sayin would be out "several weeks." The good news is Ohio State is off next week. The bad news is that when the Buckeyes return from their respite, they'll be on the road to face USC , and then it's a home game with Oregon . While both those teams have had their issues in 2026, the prospect of having to face both with a true freshman at QB is not one that should excite anybody in Scarlet and Gray. If Sayin is out even longer, there are games left against a Northwestern team that's now 5-1 after beating Michigan State , as well as a road game against the Nebraska team that gave Indiana fits last week. Oh, and there's Michigan too. College football can be a brutal sport. Sometimes victory can be taken from you by a toe or two; other times, it comes at a serious cost. That was the case Saturday in Ohio State's 19-15 win over Indiana , a game neither team escaped feeling whole. Indiana's 22-game win streak came to an end in an extremely painful manner. Down five late, on a fourth-and-4 at the Ohio State 27, Indiana opted to go for the throat instead of the first down. Josh Hoover dropped back, found a wide-open Nick Marsh down the sideline, and hit him in stride. After taking a vicious hit from Indiana's Mario Landino, Sayin was seen running to the Ohio State locker room, right arm hanging by his side. He emerged a few minutes later with it in a sling, as the diminutive true freshman Luke Fahey filled in for him, and the Buckeyes offense ground to a complete halt. The Buckeyes didn't manage a first down with Fahey in the game, so while they survived the trip to Bloomington, got revenge on the Hoosiers for last season's Big Ten Championship, and avoided a perilous second loss, there are suddenly concerning questions lingering around the program. While Buckeyes fans everywhere celebrate this win, they'll do so while awaiting an injury report that could determine the fate of their season.

home.headline: Michigan injury updates: Rod Moore ‘OK’ after being carted off in win
home.blurb: The Wolverines were down a second starting offensive lineman, guard Brady Norton, while center Jake Guarnera and guard Nathan Efobi both played through injuries in Saturday’s 21-18 victory at Michigan Stadium . Guarnera especially, having been listed as a game-time decision two hours before kickoff. “Everyone has something going on at this point in the season,” starting tackle Blake Frazier said. “I’m super proud of him. He was straining all week to make sure that he was giving himself the best opportunity to be out there with us today.” ANN ARBOR, Mich. — Michigan football continues to limp its way through the schedule, and the win over Penn State was no different. Michigan (4-2, 1-2 Big Ten) started backup Avery Gach at right guard while welcoming sixth offensive lineman Manuel Beigel back to the lineup. The Wolverines were able to run for a season-high 211 yards and three touchdowns, much of that coming in the second half with backup Tommy Carr at quarterback. In-game, though, the Wolverines had to deal with a couple of scares. Safety Rod Moore had to be carted off the field in the third quarter after intercepting a Rocco Becht pass; his first turnover of the season. “Should be OK,” Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham said. “It’s nothing major. Now, will he be ready for the next game? That’s debatable, but it’s nothing that’s long term.” That’s good news for Moore, who returned in full this season following a two-year rehab from a torn ACL and meniscus in his knee. He’s started all six games this season and is one of two captains on defense. Meanwhile, cornerback Jyaire Hill was missing in the secondary toward the end of the game, and Whittingham suggested an injury kept him from playing. “But it doesn’t appear to be anything — kind of like Rod — long term,” Whittingham said. Hill struggled in coverage against Penn State receiver Chase Sowell, who caught 11 passes for 151 yards and a touchdown and drew a pair of holding penalties against the senior defensive back. “That receiver is a good receiver,” Whittingham said. “A big, physical kid. I thought we were a little soft in pass defense this game. We needed to get up and challenge a little more, get in the receiver’s face and be a little bit more aggressive in that respect.” To illustrate how beaten up Michigan is, Whittingham said as many as six starters would have been sidelined last week had the Wolverines played a game. They were on a bye instead, giving the team enough time to get some players back in time. “It was good to get those guys healthy and be able to get them to this game and perform,” Whittingham said. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Getty Images One week after stunning No. 1 Georgia , Auburn will try to replicate that effort against No. 18 LSU . Auburn will have the Jordan-Hare Stadium crowd on it side, but the team faces an uphill battle in the pursuit of two major upsets. Going into its open date, Auburn was coming off a loss to Tennessee and needed something to build upon. An upset of the No. 1 team in the country on the road will certainly suffice, and now Alex Golesh must find a way to sustain that momentum. If Auburn is going to give itself a shot to slay SEC dragons in consecutive weeks, it will need to put the game on the shoulders of Byrum Brown again. He totaled 265 yards and a pair of touchdowns against the Bulldogs. On the other hand, LSU will have to be wary of entering a hostile environment given its recent history. The team has lost both of its road games this season, and Lane Kiffin's struggles away from home date back to when he first accepted the Ole Miss job. The Baton Rouge-based Tigers just shut out a shorthanded Mississippi State team in Death Valley, and Sam Leavitt played the first clean game of his LSU tenure. He'll need to replicate that performance in Auburn. Before this battle of the Tigers begins, we have everything you need to know about the matchup. LSU vs. Auburn: Need to know LSU's road woes: LSU is the clear favorite in this game, but it has struggled to win road games lately. The Tigers have dropped eight straight road games, which is the third-longest streak in school history. LSU is 0-2 on the road this fall, and Kiffin hasn't fared well away from home throughout his SEC coaching career. Between stops at Tennessee, Ole Miss and LSU, Kiffin is 14-16. Winning on the road is hard, but LSU can't make it even harder. Run, Bryum, run: If Auburn is going to put its best foot forward this weekend -- and for the rest of the season -- Brown will have to use his legs to create offense. That worked last week in Athens, as Brown toted the rock on 26 attempts, which included five sacks. The catch is that Brown will be exposed to more hits, which increases his risk for injury. Because of that, if Auburn can get its traditional run game rolling, that takes some of the workload off Brown's legs. Auburn trying to go back-to-back: Can Auburn pull off two stunners in a row? The Tigers haven't picked up wins over ranked teams in consecutive weeks since they rattled off three straight against Georgia, Alabama and Missouri in 2013. The trouble is that Auburn hasn't played well at home against ranked opponents of late, which is somewhat surprising given the general mystique around Jordan-Hare Stadium. The team is 1-9 in its last 10 home games against top-25 teams. Where to watch LSU vs. Auburn live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Jordan-Hare Stadium -- Auburn, Alabama TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) LSU vs. Auburn prediction, picks What Auburn did last week will be commendable -- and fans will remember it forever -- but it was also extremely improbable. Georgia out-gained Auburn by 74 yards, and the Tigers barely pulled out a win despite a plus-3 turnover margin. LSU's defense is athletic enough to contain Brown, and the offense is capable of putting up big numbers. It's possible the crowd and Auburn defense give Sam Leavitt trouble, but LSU is capable of winning this game by double-digits. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Sam Leavitt of LSU and Byrum Brown of Auburn Last week's upset makes the home dog easy to sell, but our LSU vs Auburn predictions are built around the larger mismatch. The LSU Tigers bring the country's best opponent-adjusted net EPA profile to Jordan-Hare Stadium, while the Auburn Tigers still need Byrum Brown to manufacture too much of the offense himself. I'm laying the points with LSU and grabbing the Under as my best bet in this Tigers vs Tigers affair. Head over to our latest college football picks for more Week 8 betting analysis. Who will win LSU vs Auburn: LSU -7.5 I would play the LSU Tigers to 50%. Last week's win over the No. 1 Georgia Bulldogs absolutely raises the Auburn Tigers ' ceiling, but it took 26 Byrum Brown carries and three Gunner Stockton turnovers to pull it off. Additionally, Auburn is coming off one of its biggest wins in recent memory. I'm not here to tell you that LSU is a better football team than Georgia, but its profile may be more suitable for this matchup. The visitors sit No. 1 nationally in opponent-adjusted net EPA per play at +0.44 , while Auburn is 35th at +0.14. Brown is Auburn's engine on the ground, yet he ranks 100th among qualifying quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's a dangerous imbalance against a defense that can crowd the box and still trust its coverage. Jordan-Hare will have some real juice too, with belief injected into Auburn's season. However, LSU's down-to-down edge should create separation over 60 minutes. TOP PICK LSU vs Auburn Over/Under pick: Under 51.5 The Under is my top pick in this matchup and I'd play it to 49.5. Brown is producing 0.41 EPA per rush, fourth among qualified runners, and a heavy quarterback-run plan is the best way to keep the game close . That also bleeds clock. LSU's defense has held opponents to 4.35 yards per play and a 39.2% success rate, while Auburn's unit ranks 31st in adjusted EPA allowed and gives up 5.15 yards per snap . LSU's offense is good, but its opponent-adjusted efficiency ranks 25th rather than among the elite. Also, I still have not seen enough from Sam Leavitt to trust him to make game-defining plays. I don't think his head coach has either. LSU can control field position and reach the low 30s. Auburn landing in the teens leaves enough room for Under 51.5. LSU vs Auburn combo The prevailing theme throughout is LSU's defense. It controls the game, wins the game for the Tigers, and keeps it low-scoring throughout. That holds true early on, which is why I added the first-quarter Under to this combo beyond the previously mentioned two plays. I don't expect either team to come out guns blazing through the air due to decision-making concerns tied to the quarterback. That's particularly true early in the game when the emphasis on either to score quickly is minimal. That should keep the clock running most of the first quarter and start off this heavily correlated combo out strong. Can the Auburn Tigers pull off another upset in Year 1 under coach Alex Golesh? Auburn pulled off the biggest upset of the college football season by defeating No. 1 Georgia this past Saturday in Athens. Now, it turns its attention to the LSU Tigers as a team with confidence that has proven it can beat anyone. Auburn enters this game as the underdog. Correspondingly, the ESPN matchup predictor gives Auburn a 28.8% chance to win. Auburn will need to play the type of game it did against Georgia. It will need to control the line of scrimmage and consistently run the football. Auburn outgained Georgia 192-113 on the ground. The LSU Tigers are No. 1 in the conference in run defense, allowing just 88.1 yards per game on the ground. However, the Bulldogs are No. 2 in that category, and Auburn had success with Byrum Brown and the running backs. The turnover battle will be key once again. Auburn forced three turnovers against Georgia and did not commit any. Going into that game, interceptions had been an issue for Brown with seven on the season. Auburn will be facing a quarterback in Sam Leavitt who has thrown eight interceptions this season. The Auburn defense will need to create opportunities for the offense to gain an upset victory. A big advantage for Auburn is it is at home. Both of LSU's losses were away from Baton Rouge: at Ole Miss and at Kentucky. The crowd at Jordan-Hare should be electric on Saturday after Week 7's upset win at Georgia. picks.blurb: LSU football vs Auburn score prediction, scouting report - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview Story by The Daily Advertiser LSU football vs Auburn score prediction, scouting report Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads BATON ROUGE — With Halloween right around the corner, is there a worse time to pay a visit to Jordan-Hare Stadium? Lane Kiffin and No. 17 LSU football are about find out as they travel to Auburn for a renewal of an old SEC rivalry Saturday, Oct. 24 (11 a.m. CT, ABC). One of Kiffin's coaching mentors, former Alabama and LSU head coach Nick Saban , who obviously is quite familiar with Auburn, has said he believes Auburn's football stadium haunted. Weird or "magical," as Kiffin put it earlier this week, things happen inside the venue and Auburn has snatched wins from the jaws of defeat plenty of times over the years. What the LSU coach thinks Can LSU football QB Sam Leavitt keep a clean sheet? When junior starting quarterback Sam Leavitt has avoided turnovers, LSU has easily won this season. Last time out against Mississippi State, Leavitt took care of the football and worked efficiently and smart. It paid off with a 31-0 victory. Auburn has been opportunistic this season when teams have turned the ball over. Georgia fumbled late in the game last weekend, allowing Auburn to go down and kick a game-winning field goal as time expired to pull off the upset in Athens. Kiffin said earlier this week that he and his staff will highlight the importance of ball security. "As you breakdown your losses and close losses, they're usually not as much about how many plays they make," Kiffin said. "It's more the mistakes you make, and the penalties, more false starts and more turnovers than when you play at home." LSU football offensive staff familiar with Auburn QB Byrum Brown When LSU offensive coordinator Charlie Weis Jr. was South Florida's offensive coordinator under then-head coach Jeff Scott, he helped open up the recruiting process to bring Brown to the Bulls . So Weiss is familiar with Brown's game as LSU gears up for this matchup. "Really hard player to tackle, similar to playing (South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers) that way. They're different styles, but they're really strong through a lot of arm tackles," Kiffin said of Brown. "He seems really smart by the way that he plays." Brown played for Auburn head coach Alex Golesh at South Florida before following him to The Plains out of the transfer portal. LSU offense should get plenty of opportunities It's hard to score if the offense doesn't have the ball or the ability to extend drives with it. Through six games, Auburn ranks 133rd in college football in time of possession. At 26:54, Auburn is dead-last in the SEC in time of possession. But the situation is not quite like that with Ole Miss , which is second-to-last in the league in time of possession because it operates and scores quickly. Auburn scores just 26.8 points per game, which comes in 13th out of 16 teams in the SEC. While Auburn does convert third downs 46% of the time, its offense only converts touchdowns in the red zone at a 65% clip. Defenses have racked up 23 sacks against Auburn and have caused 15 Auburn turnovers to this point. All of that adds up to LSU's offense likely winning the time of possession battle. The onus, then, will be on LSU to cap drives with points. Lane Kiffin vs first-year head coaches this season It's a small sample size, but Kiffin has not found success against teams with first-year head coaches this season. It also happens that the two matchups with coaches in their first year at their programs were LSU's two road games so far this season. Still, LSU lost both of those road games at Ole Miss against Pete Golding and at Kentucky against Will Stein. That same trend is presenting itself Kiffin again, this time it's Golesh at Auburn. Golesh was the coach at South Florida from 2023 to 2025 before taking the Auburn job over the offseason. While at USF, Golesh hosted Saban and Alabama in 2023 and pushed the Crimson Tide to the brink before falling 17-3. So, this game likely won't be easy for LSU. Kiffin will look to buck the trend against Golesh at Auburn this weekend. LSU football vs Auburn prediction If you are a believer in trap games or letdown spots, LSU's road game at Auburn is a hard game to handicap. One could argue this is a trap game for LSU — also factor that this game kicks of at 11 a.m. — while Auburn comes into the showdown off the program's biggest win in some time, knocking off No. 1 Georgia on the road. Only thing that feels certain about this game is that Jordan-Hare will be rocking and odd things take place in that building. Look for an ugly, sloppy, sleepy game. LSU squeaks one out in the end. As it stands, the Tigers are a seven-point underdog to their rival Tigers, though CBS Sports' Austin Nivison believes the Tigers will lose by at least 10 points . Here's why. "What Auburn did last week will be commendable -- and fans will remember it forever -- but it was also extremely improbable," he wrote. "Georgia out-gained Auburn by 74 yards, and the Tigers barely pulled out a win despite a plus-3 turnover margin. LSU's defense is athletic enough to contain Brown, and the offense is capable of putting up big numbers. It's possible the crowd and Auburn defense give Sam Leavitt trouble, but LSU is capable of winning this game by double digits." In fact, every CBS analyst polled about the game took Lane Kiffin's squad to win straight-up, but a few, like Chip Patterson and David Cobb, predicted the Tigers to at least cover the spread. It's certainly a difficult matchup for the Tigers, who could be experiencing what Kiffin called 'relief syndrome' after their win against Georgia. There is a path to the Tigers winning this game, though, and it seems to run through Byrum Brown. "If Auburn is going to put its best foot forward this weekend -- and for the rest of the season -- Brown will have to use his legs to create offense," Nivison continued. "That worked last week in Athens... The catch is that Brown will be exposed to more hits, which increases his risk for injury. Because of that, if Auburn can get its traditional run game rolling, that takes some of the workload off Brown's legs." Brown seemed to have been contained a bit in earlier games, as his number was called for design plays quite rarely, but against the Dawgs, Auburn offensive coordinator Joel Gordon leaned on Brown's legs to get the Tigers' offense moving. It worked to great effect last week, but LSU will now be even more prepared for Brown's dual-threat nature, which adds a layer of complexity to the Tigers' playcalling this week. The Tigers, coming off a marquee win, are looking to continue their momentum, and having home-field advantage should play a big part in their matchup with Kiffin's Tigers. However, LSU has answers for most of Auburn's offensive production, so the Tigers will likely need to get creative if they want to emerge from the Tiger Bowl with a win. LSU enters Saturday's game at Auburn with a 5-2 overall record and 2-2 in SEC play. That's not the start Tigers fans were expecting in Lane Kiffin's debut season as head coach. LSU opened with two straight wins, including an impressive 51-10 victory over Clemson in the season opener, but then fell 32-24 at Ole Miss. They rebounded with convincing wins over Texas A&M and McNeese State, only to suffer another painful loss, falling 35-34 to Kentucky in overtime. LSU bounced back, though, with a 31-0 shutout of Mississippi State last weekend. Still, with two losses already, LSU doesn't have much room for error if they want to make the College Football Playoff . They're ranked No. 18 nationally and have remaining games against No. 13 Alabama, No. 19 Texas, at No. 11 Tennessee, and at Arkansas. They need to start winning consistently against SEC opponents, especially on the road. Thankfully for Kiffin's side, they've received some good news on two star players before the crucial Auburn matchup. Edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen and tight end Trey'Dez Green were both absent from Wednesday's initial SEC injury report, putting them on track to play Saturday. More news : Kentucky HC Will Stein Makes Feelings Clear on 24-Team College Football Playoff Umanmielen has been LSU's most impactful defender this season. Through seven games, he's already recorded eight sacks, the second-most in the country, along with 27 total tackles and 11 tackles for loss, giving the Tigers an explosive presence off the edge. Umanmielen left last week's win over the Bulldogs with a head injury after playing just seven defensive snaps. Green, meanwhile, would provide a massive boost to the offense. Before injuring his knee against Ole Miss, the star tight end had caught 14 passes for 222 yards and one touchdown in just three games. At a whopping 6-foot-7, 237 pounds, his size and ability to make plays down the field gives Sam Leavitt another reliable target. Umanmielen was a key piece of LSU's transfer portal class and was with Lane Kiffin at Ole Miss. LSU faces Auburn this Saturday at 11 A.M. CT. home.headline: Tigers hoping Green’s return can help spark road success at Auburn
home.blurb: Saturday morning at 11, in a contest carried on ESPN, the 18 th -ranked Tigers visit Auburn’s Jordan-Hare Stadium hoping for a breakthrough win over a team that just knocked Georgia out of the nation’s No. 1 ranking, 27-24. Speaking of imposing, LSU defensive end Princewill Umanmielen is also not listed on LSU’s injury list after being knocked out of last week’s 31-0 putdown of Mississippi State with an apparent concussion. He is second nationally with eight sacks, a statistic that will be one to watch at Auburn, whose dynamic quarterback Byrum Brown has been sacked 23 times, the most in the country, and has thrown seven interceptions. LSU (5-2, 2-2) quarterback Sam Leavitt had his most impressive statistics last week, not throwing an interception for the first time this season while competing 31 of 38 passes for 289 yards and all four Tiger TDs. His first run, in the red zone on LSU’s game-opening scoring drive, revealed he had reaggravated a right hamstring injury that limited his mobility but seems to have focused his passing accuracy. “I played a pretty easy game, just getting the ball out to my guys and have them go make plays,” said Levitt, who is also not listed on LSU’s injury report. “We did an incredible job with play calling and situational ball.” Shreveport-Bossier Journal News when you need it! Simple and Free By DOUG IRELAND, Journal Sports Can LSU carry its show on the road? Not so far this season, though in the bottom line, the Tigers could have won both road games, a 32-24 loss at No. 8 Ole Miss and a 35-34 overtime defeat at No. 12 Kentucky. Not recently. LSU has dropped its last eight games outside of Tiger Stadium, six under former coach Brian Kelly. It appears likely LSU coach Lane Kiffin will have two of his best players back in the lineup. Junior tight end Trey’Dez Green is no longer on the Southeastern Conference injury list, apparently recovered from a knee injury that benched him for four games. “He battled and got himself back even quicker than they thought he’d be back,” said Kiffin on his radio show Thursday night. “He worked so hard, and he loves LSU so much.” Green, an imposing target at 6-foot-7, caught 14 passes for 222 yards and a touchdown in three games before his injury in the fourth quarter at Ole Miss, five weeks ago. But Brown focused on running the ball at Georgia and between called plays and scrambles, posted 115 yards and a touchdown on 26 carries. The transfer from South Florida, named this week as one of 18 finalists for the Campbell Trophy – considered the academic Heisman – also threw a TD pass while going 15 of 26 for 150 yards. Auburn (4-2 overall, 2-2 SEC) also got a score on a trick play, when receiver Christian Neptune put the Tigers on the board with a 28-yard pass, his second TD throw of the season. The Auburn defense came up with three turnovers. The Tigers are a 7.5-point favorite to halt their disappointments on the road heading into an open date on Halloween, with November’s slate of Alaba

By Rowan Fisher-Shotton 0 Share Newsweek is a Trust Project member See more of our trusted coverage when you search. Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search. LSU enters Saturday's game at Auburn with a 5-2 overall record and 2-2 in SEC play. That's not the start Tigers fans were expecting in Lane Kiffin's debut season as head coach. LSU opened with two straight wins, including an impressive 51-10 victory over Clemson in the season opener, but then fell 32-24 at Ole Miss. They rebounded with convincing wins over Texas A&M and McNeese State, only to suffer another painful loss, falling 35-34 to Kentucky in overtime. LSU bounced back, though, with a 31-0 shutout of Mississippi State last weekend. Still, with two losses already, LSU doesn't have much room for error if they want to make the College Football Playoff . They're ranked No. 18 nationally and have remaining games against No. 13 Alabama, No. 19 Texas, at No. 11 Tennessee, and at Arkansas. They need to start winning consistently against SEC opponents, especially on the road. Thankfully for Kiffin's side, they've received some good news on two star players before the crucial Auburn matchup. Edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen and tight end Trey'Dez Green were both absent from Wednesday's initial SEC injury report, putting them on track to play Saturday. More news : Kentucky HC Will Stein Makes Feelings Clear on 24-Team College Football Playoff Umanmielen has been LSU's most impactful defender this season. Through seven games, he's already recorded eight sacks, the second-most in the country, along with 27 total tackles and 11 tackles for loss, giving the Tigers an explosive presence off the edge. Umanmielen left last week's win over the Bulldogs with a head injury after playing just seven defensive snaps. Green, meanwhile, would provide a massive boost to the offense. Before injuring his knee against Ole Miss, the star tight end had caught 14 passes for 222 yards and one touchdown in just three games. At a whopping 6-foot-7, 237 pounds, his size and ability to make plays down the field gives Sam Leavitt another reliable target. home.headline: LSU football DE Princewill Umanmielen on track to play vs Auburn
home.blurb: LSU football expects to have its pass rusher available when the Tigers travel to face Auburn on Saturday. LSU defensive end Princewill Umanmielen was absent from the Wednesday injury report, a good sign after Umanmielen left LSU's win over Mississippi State and did not return. LSU's defense was already dealing with the injury bug. Defensive back Da'Shawn Spears tore his ACL vs. Ole Miss and will miss the entire season, while linebacker Whit Weeks is missing an extended period and won't return until November. If LSU were without Umanmielen, the Tigers would be down yet another impact player. LSU managed fine after Umanmielen left the Mississippi State game, going to win 31-0, but LSU's defensive end depth is a question mark, and Umanmielen is an All-American-caliber player. LSU's pass rush is elite with Umanmielen on the field. Umanmielen has eight sacks and 22 pressures in 2026. He also makes an impact against the run, with six run stops this year. Umanmielen was a key piece of LSU's transfer portal class and was with Lane Kiffin at Ole Miss. LSU faces Auburn this Saturday at 11 A.M. CT. The 5-2 Tigers need a win to keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive. This article originally appeared on LSU Wire: LSU football DE Princewill Umanmielen on track to play vs Auburn

Pete Fiutak Fri, October 23, 2026 at 6:10 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads All of a sudden, South Carolina has become the proverbial Team You Don't Want To Face. It was only one game a few weeks ago in horrendous conditions, but the Gamecocks' 38-19 win over Florida showed one thing more than anything else – they're still trying. This was supposed to be a big bounceback season for South Carolina, but it lost three straight SEC games, including an overtime home game to Kentucky, and that was it. No SEC title, no CFP appearance. It was all over, and it wasn't even the second week of October. This is a good Gamecock team in the fun make-lemonade-out-of-the-season position of getting to screw everyone else up. Tennessee has to keep its focus and show that it's worthy of being in the mix for all the things South Carolina was supposed to be fighting for right now. It beat Alabama, it took out Auburn by ten, and it probably should've beaten Texas. Now it has to sidestep the landmine. Tennessee vs South Carolina: Quick Hits The Vols get a week off before hosting Kentucky, and then they're off to Texas A&M. South Carolina goes to Oklahoma next week before hosting Texas A&M. The two haven't played since Tennessee won 41-20 in 2023. The Vols are 4-1 in the last five meetings. How To Watch Tennessee vs South Carolina Date: Saturday, October 24, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: FS1 Location: Williams-Brice Stadium, Columbia, SC – Week 8 Schedule & Predictions – What Will the CFP 12-Seed Bracket Be? – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – CFN Expert Picks: Week 8 Why Tennessee Will Win Pass rush, pass rush, pass rush, pass rush, pass rush . The Tennessee running game was okay in the win over Alabama, and George MacIntyre kept his cool, throwing for close to 200 yards. But the offense turned it over twice and was hardly smooth. The Volunteer defense held Bama to 201 yards of total offense and forced four takeaways because of the ten tackles for loss and five sacks that dominated the game. Tennessee is No. 1 in the nation in sacks, and it's about to force the Gamecocks into a whole slew of mistakes. Why South Carolina Will Win How did South Carolina blow out Florida? LaNorris Sellers showed the upside to be a dangerous NFL quarterback. The offense didn't turn the ball over, and the defense pitched a gem, especially against the run. Tennessee has a good offense, but it's the defense that delivers the mail. South Carolina can't get frustrated. It needs to keep the mistakes to a bare minimum and be okay with living to fight another day. Tennessee vs South Carolina Prediction, Betting Lines It is possible to run on the Tennessee defense. It'll get its sacks and plays behind the line, but Auburn was able to run well against the Vols. It lost because it turned the ball over three times. Arch Manning was actually okay against the Vols, but the two Texas turnovers and 11 penalties made it way too close. The weather had a lot to do with the three Florida turnovers against South Carolina. It's going to be 72 and sunny on Saturday in Columbia. Published: Oct 22, 2026 · 10:00 AM EDT The Fearless Prediction had wavering confidence in Josh Heupel and the Tennessee Volunteers last week and could not have been more wrong. Tennessee's defense is absolutely legit, and the offense showed remarkable physical and mental toughness in a dominating 26-10 victory over Alabama . We won't doubt the Big Orange again. (Looks at schedule.) If you had to explain to a friend who knows nothing about college football what a “trap game” was, Tennessee's upcoming visit to South Carolina potentially fits the bill. The Vols do not play well at Williams-Brice. Tennessee's loss in 2016 put it on the road to losing the SEC East. The Vols' loss in 2022 probably cost them a spot in the 4-team College Football Playoff and saw their star QB Hendon Hooker rip up his knee, ending his college career. There's also the matter of Connor Stalions and how he may or may not have assisted South Carolina. College football rarely disappoints. In terms of this season, the Vols are coming off an impressive victory and a rivalry win, no less. Can they put that in the rearview? As for South Carolina, Shane Beamer is coaching for his job. Last time out, the Gamecocks pulled off a surprising win at Florida , and now are well rested following a bye week. Tennessee's defense is good. Really good. Following a 5-sack performance against Alabama, the Vols have 30 sacks on the season, tops in the FBS. They are also 6th in the country in tackles for loss with 58. Against the Crimson Tide, the Vols stopped 11 of 13 third-down attempts and allowed only 54 rushing yards. Defensive linemen Xavier Gilliam and Tyree Weathersby are the modern-day Undertaker and Kane, causing havoc with a combined 11.5 sacks and 18.5 tackles for loss. Linebackers Amare Campbell and Arion Carter are at the top of the tackle table with 46 and 43, respectively. The Vols have also collected 13 turnovers, tied for 10th-best in the FBS. New defensive coordinator Jim Knowles has been a revelation, leading one of the best groups in the country. As for that Tennessee offense, why don't they just build the whole plane out of DeSean Bishop? He's now averaging nearly 120 rushing yards per game with a healthy 6 yards per carry. Against Alabama, he had 159 rushing yards and 2 scores. Having Bishop takes a lot off the plate of redshirt freshman QB George MacIntyre, who seems to have cemented his place as Tennessee's starter. He'll get the call for his 2nd career road start on Saturday. As for South Carolina, the Gamecocks were left for dead a couple of weeks ago, as was their head coach, Shane Beamer. They had lost 3 straight, including a crushing OT loss to Kentucky . But then came a startling 38-19 victory over Florida. QB LaNorris Sellers has a combined 291.5 yards passing and rushing, with 14 combined TDs. South Carolina needs a big game from Sellers if it is going to win on Saturday. Tennessee doesn't give up many big plays, but needs to be aware of WR Nyck Harbor, averaging 16.4 yards per reception. RB Matt Fuller is gaining 81 yards per game on the ground. Defensively, senior LB Justin Okoronkwo leads the Gamecocks with 43 tackles. Lineman Tomiwa Durojaiye has 4.5 tackles for loss. If special teams are to be a factor, Tennessee's Cooper Ranvier has made 10 of 11 FGs, South Carolina's Malik Orsan has made 8 of 10 FGs. Weird things happen in this game, especially when played in Columbia. But Tennessee gets a break with an afternoon kickoff. That means less time for those Gamecocks fans to pregame. It's not revenge the Vols are after on Saturday… it's the reckoning. Four years ago, South Carolina fans reveled in destroying Tennessee's Playoff dreams. They won't get a repeat performance. Fearless Prediction: Tennessee 26, South Carolina 17 Mark Nagi has covered Tennessee athletics for over 20 years. He is the author of “Decade of Dysfunction,” an in-depth look at all that led to the crazy coaching search of 2017 at Tennessee. The book is available on Amazon. By Parker Gillam Published: Oct 21, 2026 · 7:58 PM EDT Tennessee is set to pay a visit to South Carolina this Saturday, and the Volunteers are still riding high following their upset win over Alabama last weekend. But Columbia has been far from kind to the Volunteers in recent memory, as they've dropped 6 of their last 8 contests at Williams-Brice Stadium heading into this one. That was one of the many points ESPN's Greg McElroy made in his breakdown of the game during an episode of his “Always College Football” show, and the former Alabama quarterback is actually picking the Gamecocks to pull off the upset. “I'm gonna take South Carolina to win this game, 27-24, and I think they're gonna do it on the ground,” McElroy said . “They're also coming off a bye. Tennessee just went to war, and looked amazing doing it. But we've seen teams elevate and then come back down to Earth the following week, and I think that's what's gonna happen here.” RELATED: Looking for the latest spreads and totals? Check out the current college football odds before you bet. McElroy elaborated by saying that LaNorris Sellers and Matt Fuller will be able to find plenty of success on the ground, with him adding that South Carolina ‘s downfield weapons will create enough explosive plays to counteract anything Tennessee throws at them. “Tennessee linebackers cannot afford to miss in this game,” McElroy said. “Because that would keep the Gamecocks out of third and long, which is where Tennessee's sacks live.” Parker is currently the sports editor for Gulf Coast Media in Foley, Alabama. He's a graduate from Mizzou who has experience covering the Tiger football and basketball beats for SB Nation, and he's worked for a variety of sports news outlets in the past. away.blurb: The Wildcats are in desperate need of someone to step in for Oakley. He was the leading receiver at the position for K-State a year ago. This season, he is among the top players on the roster with NFL interest. During training camp, Klein said he hosted several NFL scouts who were on campus to check out Oakley. Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Shandel Richardson Tue, October 20, 2026 at 3:50 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas State Wildcats are expected to once again be without one of their key offensive players this weekend on the road against the Arizona State Sun Devils. K-State coach Collin Klein hinted that tight end Garrett Oakley could miss the third game of the Big 12 conference schedule. Oakley did not play in last week's game against the Kansas Jayhawks in the Sunflower Showdown at Bill Snyder Family Stadium. Here's what Klein had to say during his weekly press conference about the Oakley situation. "Probably unlikely, but we'll see," Klein said. "Day to day." Oakley missed the game because of an undisclosed illness. It gave more opportunities to sophomore Linkon Cure, who is among the most hyped players in program history. He is the first five-star recruit to ever play at Kansas State. While he has gotten off to a slow start, the Wildcats are hoping he can live up to the huge expectations. He has seven catches for 66 yards this season. Last week he caught two passes for 16 yards. The Wildcats need production from Cure because Oakley isn't the only tight end missing. Two weeks ago, it was announced that backup Will Anciaux would miss the season after sustaining a lower leg injury. Klein is also experimenting with moving left tackle Oliver Miller to tight end. That's where he played last week in the win against the Jayhawks. It is unknown if the move is permanent but that's where Miller will play this week. This was a move that was in the works because the Wildcats coaching staff was using him at tight end the past few weeks. A 6-foot-6 freshman, Miller has embraced the opportunity. He was a standout at Cherry Creek (Colo.) High School, where he was rated the No. 41 tackle in the country. Perhaps this could be a better calling for him because of his athleticism. The hope is Oakley is back in uniform sooner than later. He is a big component of the offense and is needed if the Wildcats are going to remain in the hunt for the Big 12 conference championship and College Football Playoff.

picks.headline: What an Advanced Model Predicts in Clemson's ACC Matchup with Virginia Tech
picks.blurb: What an Advanced Model Predicts in Clemson's ACC Matchup with Virginia Tech Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2025 FOOTBALL BRACKET BASKETBALL NEWS Saturday night marks a crossroads for the Clemson Tigers and head coach Dabo Swinney, who welcome in the Virginia Tech Hokies in a highly-anticpated matchup. Memorial Stadium should be sold out this weekend, and Swinney will look to continue the strong stretch coming out of the open date. However, when looking at the advanced analytics, it could mean that Clemson has to survive a strong test from the Hokies to pick up its third ACC win of the season. Fortunately for fans, there tends to be a lean towards the Tigers in that department, according to Versus Sports Simulator . It gives Clemson a 64% chance to win on Saturday, with an average score being around 29-23. This contest has been one that has constantly switched in the projections, due to the losses that both teams have had since the month of October began. Virginia Tech had a two-game skid against Pitt and Cal, losing by a score in both games, to be forced to win out for the remainder of the season. However, when the month began, the Tigers only had a 53% chance to win. The model gives Swinney’s group a defense with a B+ grade, while the offense is generously given a B- grade. That’s how Clemson has won games over the course of this season, with the defense leaving enough points on the board for the Tigers to score on sporadic occasions. On the flip side, Virginia Tech is given a C+ overall ranking by Versus, with its best quality being a B- offense. However, it’s important to note that the Hokies’ defense, although graded a C+, leads the country in tackles for loss and is also first in the ACC in sacks and forced fumbles. Regardless, Clemson is expected to hit the ground running, with this amount being the most it has scored against a Power Four opponent at all this season. The home-field advantage plays a small factor in the Tigers' favor, with betting markets having them favored by about a field goal. Even with the game being at Memorial Stadium, Versus has Clemson as the favorite regardless of where the game is. If the game were at Lane Stadium, Swinney’s group would have a 52% chance to win the game on Saturday. However, there’s much more to a game than the model itself, but the advanced analytics show advantages on Clemson’s end that perhaps others aren’t thinking about. Swinney will look to reinforce that at home on Saturday, playing a team that will be playing with hopes to remain in the ACC Championship contention pool. Kickoff is set for 7 p.m. and the game will be broadcast on ESPN. picks.blurb: Virginia Tech's Ethan Grunkemeyer leads the Hokies into Memorial Stadium, less than a year after he squared off against the Tigers in the Pinstripe Bowl at Yankee Stadium while playing for Penn State. In that game, Grunkemeyer threw for 260 yards and two touchdowns in Penn State's 22-10 win over Clemson. A third-year QB who committed to the Nittany Lions and James Franklin, Grunkemeyer followed his former Penn State coach to Blacksburg after Franklin was hired by Virginia Tech last November after the Nittany Lions parted ways with the 12-year skipper barely a month earlier. He has thrown for 1,984 yards and 15 touchdowns to two interceptions through seven games this season. Grunkemeyer and Virginia Tech lead the ACC in passing yards , though the Hokies have played one more game than Darian Mensah and the No. 1-ranked Miami Hurricanes. Clemson's passing game has been a complete contrast, to say the least. Through their first six contests, the Tigers have thrown a combined two touchdown psases between Week 1 starter Christopher Vizzina and former four-star freshman Tait Reynolds. The Tigers are second to last in the ACC in total offense with 340.7 yards per game while Virginia Tech ranks sixth (449.7) in the conference. Reynolds was 17 of 26 for 127 yards in Clemson's 37-0 win over Charleston Southern in Week 6. He has thrown for 943 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions entering his fifth start of 2026. away.blurb: BLACKSBURG — Following a win over Georgia Tech, Virginia Tech football heads out on the road to face Clemson in a pivotal ACC game. Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. The player availability report, which was first used for the 2025 season, provides five types of designations prior to game day: available, probable, questionable, doubtful, and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Eleven players are on this week's report for Virginia Tech, the same as Week 6 against Cal and Week 7 against Georgia Tech. Here's how the availability report shakes out by position: The Hokies' loss against Pitt came in spite of them racing out to an early 14-0 lead. The Panthers roared back with a 35-10 response, leading by as many as 11 in the final quarter. Though the Hokies mounted a nine-point rally, fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard game-deciding field goal was ruled no good. Initial Availability Report Released for Virginia Tech-Georgia Tech: Who's In, Out, TBD For Hokies? Here's the list of players posted on the initial availability report, organized by status: Offensive Line: 4 (Terry, Wright, Austin, Cunningham) Wide Receiver: 3 (Peterkin, Booker, Stuewe) Cornerback: 2 (Williams, Chadwick) Following its first 4-0 start since the 2017 season with wins over VMI , Old Dominion , Maryland , and Boston College , Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2 ACC) lost back-to-back clashes with Pitt and Cal. Both were by one score, marking the first time since September 2024 that the Hokies have lost back-to-back games by seven points or fewer. The following week, Virginia Tech lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley. The Hokies held a 14-13 lead entering the final quarter, allowing the Golden Bears to pull ahead. Virginia Tech scored a go-ahead touchdown with 1:15 to go, but Cal's six-play, 75-yard drive — aided by a pair of penalty calls for roughing the passer (Kaleb Spencer) and defensive pass interference (Kenny Woseley Jr.) — enabled it to score the game-winning touchdown with 18 seconds remaining. Virginia Tech marched the ball down to Cal's 7-yard line with three seconds remaining, but quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer's last-gasp throw to a contested Luke Reynolds was incomplete. The Hokies bounced back last week, though, with a 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech in Lane Stadium. Virginia Tech held a 24-3 lead at intermission and despite being outscored by 11 in the second half, it held firm. Grunkemeyer threw for 215 yards in the first half, though he only logged 35 more passing yards over the final two quarters. This year, Grunkemeyer's completed 72.9% of his passes for 1,984 yards (No. 4 in FBS), 15 touchdowns and two interceptions. There will be four reports in total: today's report, one report on Thursday and Friday, plus a game-day report two hours before Virginia Tech's tussle with Clemson. Freshman wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is the only newly announced absence ahead of Saturday night’s game against Virginia Tech, while most of the remaining names have been unavailable for weeks. Sellars suffered a concussion and entered protocol following what Dabo Swinney described as the freshman’s best practice of the season. Clemson will hold him out when the Tigers host the Hokies at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN. The 6-foot-3, 200-pound receiver had finally worked his way back from the hamstring issue that limited him during fall camp. Swinney said Sellars made two impressive catches during practice and had established himself as Clemson’s fourth receiver behind Bryant Wesco Jr., Tyler Brown and T.J. Moore. Virginia Tech has its own problems up front. Offensive lineman Justin Terry is out, while Nathaniel Wright, Lucas Austin, and Montavious Cunningham are questionable. The Hokies allowed seven sacks in last week’s 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech . This article originally appeared on Clemson Wire: ACC injury report for Clemson vs. Virginia Tech: Who is out? home.blurb: Clemson football's initial availability report carries 10 injuries, one being fresh. Freshman wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is the only newly announced absence ahead of Saturday night’s game against Virginia Tech, while most of the remaining names have been unavailable for weeks. Sellars suffered a concussion and entered protocol following what Dabo Swinney described as the freshman’s best practice of the season. Clemson will hold him out when the Tigers host the Hokies at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN. The 6-foot-3, 200-pound receiver had finally worked his way back from the hamstring issue that limited him during fall camp. Swinney said Sellars made two impressive catches during practice and had established himself as Clemson’s fourth receiver behind Bryant Wesco Jr., Tyler Brown and T.J. Moore. Virginia Tech has its own problems up front. Offensive lineman Justin Terry is out, while Nathaniel Wright, Lucas Austin, and Montavious Cunningham are questionable. The Hokies allowed seven sacks in last week’s 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech . This article originally appeared on Clemson Wire: ACC injury report for Clemson vs. Virginia Tech: Who is out? Sellars has only three catches for eight yards this season, so Clemson is not losing a premium part of its passing game. His absence still shortens a receiver rotation that is already missing Cole Turner and reserve Chase Byrd. Turner has been away from the program since fall camp while handling a personal matter There is some good health news from the report. Running back Jay Haynes returned against Charleston Southern for his first game action since suffering multiple knee injuries in the 2024 ACC Championship Game. Defensive tackle Kourtney Kelly also made his Clemson debut after tearing his ACL during spring practice. home.blurb: Clemson True Freshman WR Gordon Sellars III Ruled Out vs. Virginia Tech - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Clemson True Freshman WR Gordon Sellars III Ruled Out vs. Virginia Tech Clemson true freshman WR Gordon Sellars III has been ruled out for this week's contest vs. Virginia Tech due to a concussion. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Angelo Feliberty Thu, October 22, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads "Well, he had his best day yesterday, but he's gonna be out this weekend," he said. "He's got a concussion, so he'll be out unfortunately. But he had a great day; had a couple of good catches." "I thought, Gordo was a guy that came out of spring ball that I thought, 'Here we go,' and he dealt with some injuries in fall camp, and it kind of set him back," Morris said on Wednesday. "It was really good to see his speed. I thought he flashed." "You know, he's really kind of been that next guy, and that's really been since the spring," he finished. "He just kind of emerged, and then he pulled his hamstring in camp and has kind of been limited a good bit, but has been able to play some and kind of been working his way back." As it stands, there's no clear timetable for Sellars' return, but true freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds will still have plenty of weapons in the Week 8 conference matchup, with Bryant Wesco Jr. and T.J. Moore ready to get back on track. This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/clemson as Clemson True Freshman WR Gordon Sellars III Ruled Out vs. Virginia Tech . As the Clemson Tigers head back into ACC play against Virginia Tech this weekend, they'll be without a key depth piece on the offensive side of the ball. Speaking during media availability on Wednesday, head coach Dabo Swinney announced that true freshman wideout Gordon Sellars III will miss the Week 8 contest vs. the Hokies due to a concussion he suffered in practice on Tuesday. As we reported earlier this season, Sellars has been a standout , not just among the freshmen but among the receivers as a whole, taking over as the primary backup on the outside while sophomore Juju Preston fills the backup slot role. It's an untimely setback for a freshman who has been trending up, and one that offensive coordinator Chad Morris says he saw coming back during the spring period. Swinney shared a similar view, and the concussion is especially frustrating for a young talent who worked hard to come back from the hamstring injury Morris referenced during fall camp. Not to mention, junior tight end Christian Bentancur is coming off a career-high four catches for 74 yards against Charleston Southern in Week 7. So we'll see if Morris continues to open up the playbook for pass-catching outside of receivers. Swinney and the Tigers are set to kick off from Memorial Stadium at 7 p.m. ET, and the game will be broadcast on E
